FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Part 4) was adopted by Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by the AYUSH 
Sectional Committee was had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 


There is a worldwide resurgence of interest in holistic systems of health care, particularly with respect to the 
prevention and management of lifestyle-related disorders, chronic, non-communicable and systemic diseases. It is 
increasingly understood that no single health care system can provide satisfactory answers to all the health needs 
of modern society. Evidently there is a need for a new inclusive and integrated health care regime that should 
guide health policies and programmes in future. 


This Indian Standard is published in four parts. The other parts in the series are: 


Part 1 Standardized terminology for fundamental principles 
Part 2 Standardized terminology for diagnosis and etiological factors 
Part 3 Standardized terminology for foods and beverages 


Ayurveda is a comprehensive scientific system of medicine evolved in India. Initially it was developed through 
ancient wisdom, clinical experiences and experimentation in scientific manner. At present, Ayurveda is growing in 
the paradigm of contemporary scientific, technological and medical parameters. Good health is a basic prerequisite 
to acquire materialistic, social and spiritual upliftment of individual. Ayurveda lays great emphasis on preservation 
and promotion of health and prevention of disease. This is achieved through lifestyle management complimented 
with other interventions including drugs and specialized procedures. 


The earliest concepts of Ayurvedic science are found in the ancient texts called Vedas, which are believed to 
be composed between 5000 and 1000 BC. The classical texts of Ayurveda containing exclusive information 
on health and disease came around 1000 B.C. onwards, when fundamental and applied principles of 
Ayurveda were documented in a systematic manner. 


The Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given at Annex A. 


There are several technical terms which are specific to Ayurveda including the terminology pertaining to 
Fundamentals of Ayurveda, Ayurvedic Pharmacology & Pharmacognosy, Structure and Function of human body 
as per Ayurveda, Diagnosis & Etiological factors in Ayurveda, Signs and Symptoms, Treatment modalities, 
preparation of medicines, foods & beverages, etc. The inputs have been derived from information available in the 
public domain in print and electronic media inter-alia the Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, NAMASTE Portal 
and authoritative books of Ayurveda. 


1 SCOPE 


This standard (Part 4) covers description/definition 
of terminologies related to medicinal preparations 
in Ayurveda. The original terms appearing in the text 
have been transliterated in English and defined for 


Indian Standard 


IS 17424 (Part 4) : 2020 


GLOSSARY OF AYURVEDIC TERMINOLOGY 


PART 4 STANDARDIZED TERMINOLOGY FOR 
MEDICINAL PREPARATIONS 


the purpose of clear understanding of the concept by 


any person who is not an expert in Ayurveda. These 
terms may be used by manufacturers, researchers, 
academicians, regulators, clinical practitioners and 
other enthusiasts interested in the science of Ayurveda. 


2 STANDARDIZED TERMINOLOGY FOR MEDICINAL PREPARATIONS 


SI No. 


Term 


English 
Transliteration 


Definition 


Aupa 


Aushadaha kalpana 


Various preparations of medicine 


Aupa 


Bhaishajya kalpana 


Ayurvedic pharmaceutics 


Rasa shastra 


Branch of Ayurvedic pharmaceutics 
in which various metals, minerals and 
other substances, including mercury, 
are purified and combined with herbs 
for therapeutic purpose 


Anupaana 


Adjunct administered either along with 
or just after the principal medicine to 
enhance its therapeutic action 


Amritikarana 


Purifying procedure to remove the 
residual impurities and to enhance the 
therapeutic action of drugs 


Kajjali 


Black mixture of mercury and sulphur 


Kaanjika 


Sour rice gruel also called as 
dhaanyaamla 


Kupipaaka 


Process by which, formulations are 
prepared by heating in a glass flask / 
bottle 


Ghana 


Thick liquid concentrate prepared 
by boiling the drug with eight or 
sixteen times of water until one-eighth 
remains. It is then filtered and boiled 
again to get a thick concentrate 


Ghanasattva 


The desired drug is washed well with 
water and cut into small pieces and 
added with four times water and boiled 
on mild heat till one-fourth water 
remains and then filtered and further 
heated till the water is evaporated and 
the decoction is reduced to a semisolid 
extract

English 
Transliteration 


Definition 


11 


qiga 


Ghritamurcchhana 


Ghrta (clarified butter) is boiled in a 
vessel till it becomes free from froth 
and cooled. The kalka (paste) of 
desired drugs is added and boiled on 
mild heat 


Chanakaamla 


Dew drops appearing on chaņa plant 
(Cicer arientinum) are collected and 
evaporated by heating until a very 
small amount remains and further 
dried by keeping the vessel under sun 
to make a powder 


EUIREJErARGJ 


Choornodaka/ Shuddhoka 


Lime water filtrate obtained by mixing 
60 ml of water with 250 mg of lime 
powder, keeping for 9 h and then 
filtering through a filter paper after 
decantation 


Nirmalikarana 


Various methods for purification of 
drug 


Dhaalana 


Process of pouring molten metal into 
specified liquid 


Tandulodaka 


Rice water obtained by mixing 48 gm 
ofrice with 385 ml of water, keeping it 
for two hours and thereafter decanting 
it. 


Tushaambu 


Barley water obtained from a mixture 
of equal quantity of crushed barley 
and warm water kept over night 


Tailamoorchhana 


Tila taila (Sesamum oil) is taken in a 
vessel and boiled till it becomes free 
from froth. It is then cooled and added 
with water and decoction of desired 
drugs and boiled till water content is 
lost. It removes the undesired smell 
from the oil 


Dhoopana 


Process of fumigating with the 
prescribed drugs 


20 


Neusa 


Niruttha/ Apunarbhava 


Property of bhasma (ash) from which 
it cannot be reverted to its metallic 
form 


21 


Nirvaapana/ Nimajjana 


Process of immersing the heated solid 
ingredients in a specified liquid 


22 


23 


Parpati 


Prakshepa 


Thin flakes prepared from kajjali by 
heating and melting it with or without 
other drugs 


Fine powder of drugs added to a drug 
dosage form to enhance palatability 
and bioavailability of the drug 


24 


Pratinidhidravya 


Drug or herbs which can be used in 
case of unavailability of the desired 
drug

Special kind of vessel used in

with burnt husk, china clay etc after

32 


Rasakriya 


Desired drug is made into decoction 
which is filtered and then concentrated 
to make a thick syrup of phaanita 
(raw jaggery) like consistency similar 
to ghana 


33 


MaRS 


Laaksharasa 


Liquid obtained by processing 
the bundled mass of Jaaksha 
(Laccifer lacca) in six times of water 
in a specific vessel called dolaayantra 
and straining it twenty one times 


34 


Sharaava 


Round shaped shallow earthen vessel 


35

Process of removal of impurities and 
potentiating of drugs 


36 


Sandhaana 


Process of fermentation of liquid with 
desired drugs 


37 


Sandhilepana 


Sealing the edges of a vessel, with the 
lid on, at the point of contact, with a 
paste of clay and cloth 


38

Supernatant liquid containing self-

Heating of desired substance in a pan 
in fire

Suaangasheeta 


When heated materials are allowed to 
self-cool 


41 


Kalpana 


Various forms of medicines 


42

Fine paste of a fresh herb

Measure of heat in terms of various

50

A type of heating arrangement using

51 


Gajaputa 


A type of heating arrangement 
wherein heating is done in a pit of 90 
cm length, breadth and depth filled 
with cow dung cakes 


52 


Varaahaputa 


A type ofheating arrangement wherein 
heating is done in a pit of 60 cm in 
length, breadth and depth filled with 
cow-dung cakes

Ardha-Gajaputa 


A type ofheating arrangement wherein 
heating is done in a pit of half the size 
of a gajaputa

Instrument; equipment; machine for

An alchemical apparatus used for

Mortar with pestle, made of various

An alchemical apparatus used for

fedturds-aa 


Tiryakapaatanayantra 


Analchemical apparatus for distillation 
of various drugs like Mercury with the

Iron ladle shaped instrument with a

SI No. 


Term 


English 
Transliteration 


Definition 


60 


Dolayantra 


An alchemical apparatus consisting of 
a pot half filled with specified liquid 
with a horizontal rod placed on the rim 
from which the bundle of material to 
be treated will be immersed and heated 


61 


Balukayantra 


Big-mouthed hollow earthen 
vessel/heating instrument filled with 
sand 


62 


URa-sPaeorR 


Paarada ashtasamskaara 


Eight main procedures used for 
purification and potentiating Paarada 
(Mercury) from its raw form to 
Paarada (Mercury) which is useful 
for medical as well as metallurgical 
procedures 


63 


Swedana 


One of the eight main procedures 
used for purification and potentiating 
Paarada (Mercury) involving sudation 
of Paarada (Mercury) -generally done 
in a dolayantra 


64 


Mardana 


One of the eight main procedures 
used for purification and potentiating 
Paarada (Mercury) involving 
trituration of Paarada (Mercury)- 
generally done in a khalvayantra 


65 


Moorchhana 


One of the eight main procedures 
used for purification and potentiating 
Paarada (Mercury) involving 
trituration of Paarada (Mercury)to the 
level so as to remove all its impurities 
and making it moorchhita (inactive) 


66 


Utthaapana 


One of the eight main procedures 
used for purification and potentiating 
Paarada (Mercury) involving 
re-potentiation of Paarada (Mercury) 
from its moorchhita (inactive) form 
using various drugs 


67 


Paatana 


One of the eight main procedures 
used for purification and potentiating 
Paarada (Mercury) involving 
distillation of  Paarada by 
three procedures-Urdhvapaatana, 
Adhahpaatana and Tiryakapaatana 
done after Utthapana 


68 


Swot 


Urdhvapaatana 


Sub-type of Paatana wherein 
distillation is done in upward direction 


69 


SUA 


Adhahpaatana 


Sub-type of Paatana wherein 
distillation is done in downward 
direction 


70 


Ad- 


Tiryakapaatana 


Sub-type of Paatana wherein 
distillation is done in oblique direction

English 
Transliteration 


Definition 


71 


TARA 


Bodhana/ Rodhana 


One of the eight main procedures 
used for purification and potentiating 
Paarada (Mercury) involving removal 
of impotency of Paarada (Mercury) 
by reducing impurities which occur 
due to the previous purificatory 
procedures done on it. 


72 


Niyamana 


One of the eight main procedures 
used for purification and potentiating 
Paarada (Mercury) wherein paste of 
various drugs with Paarada (Mercury) 
is kept in desired liquid and is bundled 
in a piece of cloth and is subjected to 
sudation by Dolayantra to control its 
mobility which was imparted due to 
the previous step called Bodhana 


73 


duid 


Deepana/ Sandeepana 


Paarada (Mercury) after Niyaman 
procedure is mixed with various herbs 
and subjected to sudation in dolayantra 
to make it capable of swallowing, 
digesting or amalgamating with other 
entities 


74 


Maana 


Various nomenclatures used for 
measurement in different forms like 
length, weight and volume 


75 


Bhaara/ Pautavamaana

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: FAD 26 (15401).
